purpose: Owner decisions for the proposed multi-sport simulation portfolio. Defaults are recommendations, not accepted behavior.

questions.question: Which eligible positions may fill each NFL flex slot, and are there limits on the number of players from one position group?
questions.recommended_default: Use the current NFL roster rules already encoded in the simulator as the baseline; document them precisely before changing them.
questions.cost_if_wrong: A wrong flex definition changes draft eligibility, replacement values, roster composition, and simulation outcomes.

questions.question: What should an NFL player's overall rating mean: projected value for the next season, peak ability, or a blended football skill score?
questions.recommended_default: Keep the current rating meaning for V21; define any new all-time rating separately.
questions.cost_if_wrong: Changing the meaning of a rating can make every existing weight and historical comparison misleading.

questions.question: Which NFL schedule, seeding, tie, and playoff ruleset should the current simulation represent, and how should that version be labeled?
questions.recommended_default: Use one named real-world season ruleset and make the season year explicit in each run.
questions.cost_if_wrong: A run may be described as a current-season simulation while using incompatible schedule or playoff rules.

questions.question: Should NFL all-time ratings represent peak season, best multi-year prime, career value, or an explicit blend?
questions.recommended_default: Use a documented blend of peak and sustained prime only if the Owner wants a balanced all-time roster; otherwise choose one clear interpretation.
questions.cost_if_wrong: The pool can mix incomparable concepts, and the simulation may reward longevity or peak ability unintentionally.

questions.question: Does the approximate 1,200-player target apply to NFL alone, and what qualifies a current player for all-time eligibility?
questions.recommended_default: Plan for roughly 1,200 NFL entries and require a documented curated inclusion decision for current players.
questions.cost_if_wrong: Candidate research effort and roster representation may be sized incorrectly.

questions.question: For eligible top current players, should the proposed minus-five adjustment affect the overall score or only selected rating dimensions?
questions.recommended_default: Store it as a named all-time mode adjustment and apply it to the overall score until a dimension-specific model is approved.
questions.cost_if_wrong: A broad adjustment can unfairly weaken a player in roles that the source ratings do not measure equally.

questions.question: Should the NBA user draft a team and assign a starting five, or should the engine choose the lineup and rotation from the drafted roster?
questions.recommended_default: Let users draft a roster and offer a clear, editable lineup/rotation step before simulation.
questions.cost_if_wrong: This defines the central user interaction and changes how player ratings must represent fit and role.

questions.question: Should NBA lineup eligibility use fixed positions, multi-position labels, or skill-based roles with position as descriptive metadata?
questions.recommended_default: Use multi-position eligibility with role/skill attributes; avoid a single rigid position where modern players routinely fill multiple roles.
questions.cost_if_wrong: Incorrect position assumptions can distort lineup fit and undervalue versatile players.

questions.question: Which factors must the first NBA game model represent: lineup fit, minutes, fatigue, injuries, usage, coaching, or only player strength?
questions.recommended_default: Start with lineup fit, minutes, and player strength; add fatigue or injury effects only when they can be explained and tested.
questions.cost_if_wrong: Too little detail may feel shallow; too much can make the first version hard to tune and verify.

questions.question: Which NBA2K edition and rating fields should be the source baseline, and how should their scale map to the simulator attributes?
questions.recommended_default: Choose one edition and roster update, preserve all raw values, then review a small mapping sample before importing the full pool.
questions.cost_if_wrong: Mixing editions or mapping incompatible fields can create systematic ratings errors.

questions.question: Which NBA season and playoff format should the first current simulation represent?
questions.recommended_default: Choose one named season and encode its schedule and playoff rules as versioned configuration.
questions.cost_if_wrong: Schedule and playoff outputs may not correspond to the stated season.

questions.question: Should NBA all-time players be rated at their best season, best multi-year prime, career value, or an explicit blend?
questions.recommended_default: Use a player’s defined prime as the base, with the selected season or years recorded for each rating.
questions.cost_if_wrong: Career longevity, peak dominance, and cross-era comparability lead to very different player pools.

questions.question: How should NBA players from different rules and playing eras be compared in the all-time simulation?
questions.recommended_default: Keep source/era information and simulation-era adjustment separate, then compare transparent options on representative player examples.
questions.cost_if_wrong: One implicit era adjustment can systematically favor or penalize a generation.

questions.question: Should the proposed minus-five current-player adjustment also apply to NBA all-time candidates, and what is the eligible current-player threshold?
questions.recommended_default: Apply no adjustment until the Owner defines eligibility and confirms the NFL suggestion should also govern NBA.
questions.cost_if_wrong: Copying a football policy into basketball may misrepresent the Owner’s intent.

questions.question: Does the approximately 1,200-player target apply separately to NBA, and should candidates be balanced by position, era, or prominence?
questions.recommended_default: Plan for approximately 1,200 NBA entries and review coverage across role, era, and level of evidence.
questions.cost_if_wrong: The pool may be too small, too large, or overrepresent one role or generation.

questions.question: What does a soccer draft-season simulation mean: a fantasy-style draft, a club squad-building exercise, a transfer-window simulation, or another format?
questions.recommended_default: Prototype a fantasy-style squad draft first because it maps most directly to the existing draft-season product flow, but label it clearly as a game format rather than a real transfer model.
questions.cost_if_wrong: A draft concept that does not match how the Owner imagines soccer squad building may shape the wrong data and engine.

questions.question: Should the soccer launch list use the dated men’s domestic league ranking snapshot in the proposal, with women’s leagues and cups considered separately?
questions.recommended_default: Use the stated snapshot as a provisional scope and revalidate it before implementation.
questions.cost_if_wrong: The number and identity of competitions can change, and a ranking is not necessarily the Owner’s preferred product boundary.

questions.question: Does approximately 1,200 all-time players mean 1,200 candidates for each of NFL and NBA, or 1,200 combined?
questions.recommended_default: Plan for approximately 1,200 per sport because each sport has its own pool and rating system.
questions.cost_if_wrong: This changes the data collection effort, storage estimates, and representation targets substantially.

questions.question: Should the first shared platform boundary be limited to the web shell and run metadata, with engines remaining sport-specific?
questions.recommended_default: Yes; share only proven UI and run contracts until a second sport demonstrates a useful common abstraction.
questions.cost_if_wrong: A universal engine could entangle sport rules, while no shared shell would multiply routine product work.
